course.name: AI Trading Strategy Bootcamp
course.tagline: From 'knows pandas' to 'shipped 15+ tested strategies + live paper trading' in 13 weeks.
course.prerequisites: Solid pandas, basic Python. No finance, no math beyond high-school algebra.
course.loop: PICK -> BUILD -> BACKTEST -> BREAK -> DIAGNOSE -> LEARN CONCEPT -> REBUILD -> VERDICT -> LOG
principles: Just-in-time concepts: no math before a deliverable demands it
Every deliverable teaches exactly one thing
Failure is graded: the graveyard is a required artifact
Ship or don't advance: every week has a gate
Costs, OOS and verdicts are non-negotiable
Ugly code that runs beats pretty code that doesn't
outcomes: Spot look-ahead bias in someone else's code
Debunk a '90% win rate' strategy in 30 minutes
Test any idea end-to-end in under an hour
Reconcile live PnL vs backtest PnL

artifacts.passing_bar: 15+ strategies shipped, each with a written verdict
90 daily entries, every dead strategy autopsied

phase_retro_questions: What pattern killed the most strategies?
Which concept made the biggest difference?
What am I still fooling myself about?

strategy_ship: Runs on real data without errors
Has a written verdict (edge / no edge / inconclusive)
Has a graveyard entry if dead
week_exit: At least one concept learned (code it, explain it in 2 sentences, spot it wrong)

milestones.name: Reality check
milestones.pass_condition: Debunk a viral strategy, start to written verdict, in 30 minutes (timed and logged).

milestones.name: Backtest engine
milestones.pass_condition: Take a fresh idea from data to tearsheet + verdict end-to-end in under 30 minutes.

milestones.name: Strategy factory
milestones.pass_condition: 6 strategies tested, 3+ in the graveyard, at least 1 survivor with out-of-sample evidence.

milestones.name: Paper replication
milestones.pass_condition: 2-3 papers implemented end-to-end and compared against the paper's claims with a deviation log.

milestones.name: Live paper
milestones.pass_condition: 30 days of live paper logs plus a reconciliation report; live vs backtest divergence explained.

milestones.name: Capstone
milestones.pass_condition: Public writeup + portfolio + repo shipped; a stranger can clone the repo and understand everything.

phases.name: Engine
student_ships: Custom backtester with fees, slippage and OOS

phases.name: Strategy Factory
student_ships: 6 strategies, each with tearsheet + verdict + graveyard entry

phases.name: Paper Replication
teacher_builds: 3 paper dossiers (Time-Series Momentum, Pairs Trading, Vol-Managed Portfolios)

phases.name: Risk & Portfolio
student_ships: Sizing rules + portfolio allocation + sensitivity heatmaps

phases.name: Live Paper
student_ships: Live bot running 30 days + reconciliation report

deliverables.title: Data pipeline + validation report
deliverables.teaches: Raw prices are not data yet: fetch, cache, validate, then trust.

deliverables.title: Measurement lab: first equity curves + expectancy table
deliverables.teaches: An equity curve is the only honest scoreboard; expectancy is its atom.

deliverables.title: Viral debunk #1 (timed, 30 minutes)
deliverables.teaches: A published win rate is a marketing number until you recompute it from prices.

deliverables.title: Viral debunks #2-3 + graveyard entries
deliverables.teaches: Most 'edges' are a definition problem, a cost problem, or a sample-size problem.

deliverables.title: Backtester v1: event loop, next-bar fills, cash, positions
deliverables.teaches: A backtest is an accounting system that happens to touch markets.

deliverables.title: Cost model + cost sensitivity report
deliverables.teaches: Costs are a function of turnover: what looks like an edge is often a liquidity donation.

deliverables.title: Walk-forward/OOS runner + tearsheets + look-ahead suite green
deliverables.teaches: Out-of-sample is a process, not a number you compute once.

deliverables.title: Strategies S01-S03: MA cross, RSI reversion, Bollinger
deliverables.teaches: Signal families fail in family-specific ways; naming the family predicts the autopsy.

deliverables.title: Strategy registry + graveyard v1
deliverables.teaches: A registry turns 'I tested a bunch of stuff' into a track record.

deliverables.title: Strategies S04-S06: Donchian, momentum, pairs + bootstrap CIs
deliverables.teaches: Every backtest number is a sample from a distribution you have not seen.

deliverables.title: Overfitting audit + parameter sensitivity heatmaps
deliverables.teaches: If the edge only exists at one parameter value, the edge is in your search, not the market.

deliverables.title: Replication R1: Time-Series Momentum
deliverables.teaches: Reading a paper is an implementation task; the paper's numbers are an input, not an answer.

deliverables.title: Replication R2: Pairs Trading
deliverables.teaches: Cointegration is a relationship between two series, not a property of either one.

deliverables.title: Replication R3: Vol-Managed Portfolios + cross-paper synthesis
deliverables.teaches: Replication fidelity is a spectrum; the deviation IS the result.

deliverables.title: Risk policy: sizing rules + portfolio allocation + Monte Carlo + regime lab
deliverables.teaches: Signals decide what to trade; sizing decides whether you survive to trade it.

deliverables.title: Live harness running: broker adapter, daily signal job, dashboard
deliverables.teaches: A live bot is a boring scheduling problem wearing a finance costume.

deliverables.title: 30-day live log + reconciliation report + divergence post-mortem
deliverables.teaches: Live PnL diverges from backtest PnL in explainable, budgetable ways.

deliverables.title: Capstone: public repo + writeup + portfolio doc + roadmap
deliverables.teaches: Research you cannot explain to a stranger is research you do not understand.

concepts.name: Returns & Compounding
concepts.trigger: Your first equity curve looks like a straight line going up - until you compute what a 50% loss does to it.

concepts.name: Expectancy & Profit Factor
concepts.trigger: You cannot say whether a strategy is good; you can only say it made money.

concepts.name: Win Rate vs Edge
concepts.trigger: The '90% win rate' strategy you are debunking has a 90% win rate - and still loses.

concepts.name: Sample Size & Base Rates
concepts.trigger: Debunk #2 has 11 trades and you want to call it an edge (or a fraud) either way.

concepts.name: Annualization
concepts.trigger: Your engine prints daily numbers and every sane comparison is annual.

concepts.name: Volatility & Standard Deviation
concepts.trigger: You want to compare a 1.2%/day strategy to a 0.4%/day strategy and know if that is a lot.

concepts.name: Sharpe Ratio
concepts.trigger: Two equity curves end at the same place and you cannot tell which one was luckier.

concepts.name: Max Drawdown & Recovery
concepts.trigger: Your first engine tearsheet prints a 47% drawdown and you nearly delete the strategy.

concepts.name: Calmar & Return-vs-Pain
concepts.trigger: Two strategies with similar returns, radically different drawdowns: Sharpe says tie.

concepts.name: Transaction Costs & Slippage
concepts.trigger: Your strategy is beautiful with zero costs and dead at 10 bps round-trip.

concepts.name: Sortino & Downside Deviation
concepts.trigger: Strategy A has a better Sharpe, Strategy B never hurt you: both have the same upside.

concepts.name: Bootstrap & Confidence Intervals
concepts.trigger: Your best strategy's Sharpe is 1.4, your worst is 1.1, and you are about to rank them.

concepts.name: Parameter Sensitivity & Plateaus
concepts.trigger: You found (14, 3.5) and every neighbouring value loses money.

concepts.name: t-test Intuition
concepts.trigger: You need a decision rule for 'is this mean return distinguishable from zero'.

concepts.name: Overfitting & Walk-Forward Honesty
concepts.trigger: Your in-sample Sharpe is 2.1 and your out-of-sample Sharpe is -0.2.

concepts.name: Time-Series vs Cross-Sectional
concepts.trigger: The TSMOM paper's returns come from a mechanism your single-instrument backtests cannot express.

concepts.name: Volatility Targeting
concepts.trigger: Same signal, wildly different risk across regimes; fixed size makes your Sharpe regime-dependent.

concepts.name: Cointegration & Spreads
concepts.trigger: Two assets drift apart forever and your 'mean reversion' trade becomes a trend trade - against you.

concepts.name: Replication Deviations: Statistical vs Economic Significance
concepts.trigger: Your replication of the paper returns 60% of the paper's Sharpe and you must decide if it replicated.

concepts.name: Correlation & Portfolio Variance
concepts.trigger: Two strategies with Sharpe 1.4 and 1.2 combine into something worse than either.

concepts.name: Kelly & Fractional Kelly
concepts.trigger: You have an edge and no idea what fraction of your capital it deserves.

concepts.name: Risk of Ruin
concepts.trigger: Your optimal-f sizing has a 30% chance of halving the account before it compounds.

concepts.name: Slippage Modeling & Latency
concepts.trigger: Live fills are systematically worse than the close your backtest assumed.

concepts.name: Live vs Backtest Divergence
concepts.trigger: Live PnL is 40% below backtest PnL and you cannot tell which component ate it.

concepts.name: Regime Detection
concepts.trigger: Your whole live divergence is one volatile month, not a bug.

weeks.title: Raw Prices Are Not Data
weeks.objective: Turn a downloaded CSV into a validated dataset and a measured equity curve you can defend.
weeks.checkpoint: `make data && make validate` runs clean from a fresh clone; reports/measurement-lab.md contains an equity curve and an expectancy table computed from validated data.
weeks.graveyard_prompt: Add to the graveyard. Log the first death: the naive 'always long' and 'random entry' baselines. Cause of death is usually 'no edge, no thesis' - write it down anyway, because baseline autopsies are what future you compares against.

weeks.title: Kill Three Viral Strategies
weeks.objective: Recompute three published 'profitable strategy' claims from raw prices and write a verdict for each.
weeks.checkpoint: Milestone M1: a timed, unassisted 30-minute debunk, start to written verdict, with the timer log kept in the report.
weeks.graveyard_prompt: Expect all three to die. The graveyard entry matters more than the debunk: name the exact mechanism (look-ahead, cost denial, repainting indicator, survivorship, sample size).

weeks.title: Build the Accounting Machine
weeks.objective: Ship an event-driven backtester that converts signals into fills, cash and an equity curve without cheating.
weeks.checkpoint: Your engine passes the 8 engine unit tests and the time-travel test (positions up to T are identical whether or not future data exists), and reproduces buy-and-hold within 1% of the raw price return on SPY.
weeks.graveyard_prompt: Graveyard prompt: Your first engine will be wrong in a way you cannot see yet. Keep the broken version's equity curve; it is the exhibit for the concept on look-ahead you will write later.

weeks.title: Costs, OOS, Tearsheets
weeks.objective: Add fees and slippage, split in-sample from out-of-sample, and auto-generate a tearsheet for any strategy.
weeks.checkpoint: Milestone M2: hand yourself a fresh idea you have never tested and go from raw data to tearsheet + verdict in under 30 minutes, timed.
weeks.graveyard_prompt: Graveyard prompt: Expect at least one strategy to die the moment costs are switched on. Record the breakeven cost (bps round-trip) at which it dies; that number is the strategy's real personality.

weeks.title: The Factory Floor
weeks.objective: Run three signal families through the same pipeline and produce comparable, verdict-bearing artifacts.
weeks.checkpoint: Three strategies with tearsheets, three verdicts, a populated strategies/index.md, and at least two graveyard entries; also start the live paper clock (D0) - the 30 days must run while you work.
weeks.graveyard_prompt: Graveyard prompt: Expect the momentum/trend family to survive parameters but die on costs, and mean reversion to do the opposite. Log both mechanisms separately.

weeks.title: Six Strategies and an Honest Mirror
weeks.objective: Test three more strategy families, then attack your own best result with bootstrap, t-test and parameter perturbation.
weeks.checkpoint: Milestone M3: 6 strategies tested, 3+ in the graveyard, at least one survivor whose OOS Sharpe sits inside a bootstrap CI that excludes zero.
weeks.graveyard_prompt: The parameter heatmap is a graveyard map: log every parameter neighbourhood where the edge evaporated and name the shape (single spike vs plateau).

weeks.title: Replicate a Paper: Time-Series Momentum
weeks.objective: Implement the TSMOM result on your own data and compare your numbers to the paper's claims.
weeks.checkpoint: papers/R1_tsmom/comparison.md shows your Sharpe and the paper's Sharpe side by side, with every gap traced to a named deviation (universe, period, vol scaling, costs).
weeks.graveyard_prompt: Graveyard prompt: Replications die too. If TSMOM fails on your universe/period, that is a finding: log it with the deviation that explains it.

weeks.title: Replicate a Paper: Pairs Trading
weeks.objective: Build a cointegration-based pairs strategy, with a test for the relationship instead of a hope.
weeks.checkpoint: papers/R2_pairs/comparison.md includes the cointegration test output, the chosen pair(s), spread z-score rules, and a walk-forward run where the pair was selected only on training data.
weeks.graveyard_prompt: Graveyard prompt: Half your candidate pairs will fail the cointegration test in the OOS window. Log the failures as evidence that selection-on-full-sample is a look-ahead machine.

weeks.title: Replicate a Paper: Vol-Managed Portfolios
weeks.objective: Implement volatility targeting on a multi-asset portfolio and reconcile three replications against their papers.
weeks.checkpoint: Milestone M4: 2-3 replications shipped, each with comparison.md + deviations.md, plus papers/synthesis.md answering 'what replicated, what did not, and why'.
weeks.graveyard_prompt: Graveyard prompt: If the paper's Sharpe does not survive your costs and period, the paper is not wrong - you were not trading the paper's asset. Log the gap, not a verdict on the authors.

weeks.title: Sizing, Correlation, Survival
weeks.objective: Turn a pile of signals into a sized, correlated, survival-aware portfolio with a written risk policy.
weeks.checkpoint: reports/risk-policy.md states sizing rules in one page; the portfolio allocation beats equal-weight on the same signals, and Monte Carlo shows your ruin probability under your own rules.
weeks.graveyard_prompt: Graveyard prompt: Log the sizing rules that died: full Kelly on a fat-tailed strategy, correlation-blind diversification, vol target set so high that stops become structure.

weeks.title: Go Live (Paper)
weeks.objective: Ship a scheduled paper-trading bot that trades your risk policy, not your mood.
weeks.checkpoint: The bot runs unattended for 7 consecutive days: signals generated, orders submitted or explicitly skipped, every day logged, dashboard rebuilt - and it has been running longer than that because you started the clock in Week 5.
weeks.graveyard_prompt: Graveyard prompt: Log every operational death: missed bar, stale data, broker timeout, double order, timezone bug. Ops bugs are strategies' leading cause of death.

weeks.title: Reconcile Reality
weeks.objective: Explain every basis point of gap between your live paper PnL and your backtest's promise.
weeks.checkpoint: Milestone M5: 30+ days of live logs, a reconciliation report that attributes divergence to fees/slippage/timing/missed fills/regime, and a written expected-divergence budget for next month.
weeks.graveyard_prompt: Graveyard prompt: Any live rule you silently changed mid-run gets logged as a killed variant. Undisclosed mid-course edits are the most common way students cheat themselves.

weeks.title: Ship It in Public
weeks.objective: Publish the portfolio, the graveyard and the writeup so a stranger can clone, run and understand the whole thing.
weeks.checkpoint: Milestone M6: the stranger-clone test - a fresh clone plus a documented 15 minutes gets someone from README.md to a reproduced tearsheet; recall test passed (explain 3 concepts from memory, code 1 from scratch).
weeks.graveyard_prompt: Close the graveyard with a taxonomy: cluster all deaths into 3-5 causes and rank them. That ranked list is the most valuable artifact you built this quarter.

checks.desc: Measurement lab report with equity curve + expectancy table
You can explain compounding and expectancy in 2 sentences each and spot the wrong version in kit/spot_it_wrong.py
M1: you have demonstrably debunked a fresh viral claim in 30 timed minutes
Cost model wired into the engine
Buy-and-hold reproduction within 1% and the time-travel test passes
M2: timed end-to-end run of a fresh idea in under 30 minutes
Live paper clock started (config committed in Week 5, run in Week 11-12)
Each verdict names the mechanism of death or survival in one sentence
M3: at least one survivor whose OOS bootstrap CI excludes zero
Every gap to the paper is traced to a named deviation
Pair selection happened on training data only
Phase 4 retro written (3 questions) - see shared/retro-template.md
Ruin probability under your own rules is computed, not assumed
The bot ran unattended: no manual order edits in the log window
Writeup is published (links to the public artifact)
Stranger-clone test passed + recall test (3 concepts explained, 1 coded from scratch)

paper_dossiers.name: Time-Series Momentum
paper_dossiers.ref: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012), 'Time Series Momentum', JFE 104(2).
paper_dossiers.core_claim: Past 12-month excess return predicts the next 1-month return, for nearly every futures market, and vol-scaling makes the effect stable across regimes.

paper_dossiers.name: Pairs Trading
paper_dossiers.ref: Gatev, Goetzmann & Rouwenhorst (2006), 'Pairs Trading: Performance of a Relative-Value Arbitrage Rule', RFS 19(3).
paper_dossiers.core_claim: Form pairs on normalised historical prices, trade divergence from the spread, and the spread reverts often enough to pay for costs.

paper_dossiers.name: Vol-Managed Portfolios
paper_dossiers.ref: Moreira & Muir (2017), 'Volatility-Managed Portfolios', Journal of Finance 72(4); Harvey et al. (2018) for the replication critique.
paper_dossiers.core_claim: Scaling exposure inversely to recent realised volatility raises risk-adjusted returns, because vol clusters and returns do not scale with it.

live_paper.note: The 30-day clock is started in Week 5 precisely because it takes 30 real days. Weeks 11-12 are for engineering the harness, reconciling and writing the post-mortem - not for starting the clock.
